audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph temple musicians and courses, first-pass restored draft; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for royal and military control of music, instrumental prophecy, hereditary training, daughters' visibility, skill census, teacher-student equality, lots, and labor safeguards.

translation_notes: Military commanders participate in selecting musicians; worship must not become an arm of state or military propaganda.
Instrumental 'prophecy' reflects inspired liturgical performance, not proof every musical impression is infallible revelation.
Musicians work under fathers and king, exposing family apprenticeship and royal control; artistic consent and freedom matter.
Heman's three daughters are counted as gifts but disappear from named performance courses. Their omission should not support women's exclusion from music or spiritual authority.
Training and skill are explicitly valued; sacred music is labor requiring practice, compensation, rest, and hearing protection.
Teacher and student receive lots together, affirming equal dignity without erasing differences in responsibility.
Lots organize schedules but are not magical guarantees of justice.
Hereditary ensembles can preserve craft while also creating nepotism and pressure on children to enter family work.
safety_note: Do not militarize worship, suppress artists under royal control, exclude women, compel children into family ministries, or exploit musicians as unpaid spiritual labor. Inspiration must coexist with skill, consent, rest, and accountability.
